messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT alert: svc-infer-eu high error-rate detected (5xx) — page to @maria (oncall). Auto-escalation at 1861345678. Logs: 502 responses spiking.

maria: on it — looking at traces now. can someone post quick impact summary for customers?

devon: I see a kernel OOM pattern on a subset of pods after the recent runtime tweak. Rolling a temporary routing rule to divert to standby pool. Will patch in ~8m.

alex: applying routing change now — command: `kubectl patch svc svc-infer-eu -p '{"spec":{"sessionAffinity":"None"}}'` — switching 30% traffic to standby nodes.

li: heads-up: support is getting 3 customer reports about rate-limited failures in eu-west region (tickets #4721, #4722, #4723). Asking product for status page copy and a short customer notification draft we can send to impacted customers.

maria: devon — once routing is up, please confirm error rate drop. If we can restore within 20m, we'll treat this as a partial outage window. Need SLA eligibility calc flow.

devon: routing change completed at 1861345785. Metrics: 5xx down from 18% -> 1.3% in 3m. Keeping monitoring.

incident-bot: Metric: 5xx error_rate decreased. 5xx: 1.3% at 1861345810.

olivia: drafting status page update below — please review and sign off.

olivia: ```Status update (draft):
- Component: svc-infer-eu (text-generation)
- Incident start: 2026-04-12T10:01:18Z
- Impact: a subset of requests returned 5xx errors, causing elevated failures for customers using eu-west endpoints.
- Mitigation: traffic routed to standby pool at 10:03Z, error rates returning to normal.
- Current status: degraded → service restored to degraded (monitoring).
- Next updates: in 30 minutes or on significant changes.
```

li: looks good. Add note: "Customers using dedicated capacity were not impacted" — that helps triage billing/SLA.

olivia: updated. final draft posted to status page at 1861345880.

jamal: billing question — we need to determine SLA credit eligibility. Quick checklist: (1) measure customer-visible downtime window per route, (2) check product tier (hosted vs dedicated), (3) compute per-customer credit using committed tokens/uptime SLA. Can ops provide per-route timelines and affected percentage?

maria: confirmed: host-api eu-west experienced elevated failures from 1861345678 -> 1861345792 (approx 114s) before mitigation routing dropped impact to <2%. Dedicated instances unaffected.

devon: also note that a small fraction of long-running streams saw truncation — we should flag any customer with streaming sessions open during the window. I can export a request log with session ids.

jamal: please produce 2 outputs for billing: (A) list of impacted customers + estimated request failure fraction, (B) token-weighted downtime per customer. I'll correlate to SLA terms and prepare credit amounts.

billing-bot: Created billing case BC-2026-033 at 1861345915 assigned to @jamal.

maria: oncall handoff note for next shift (copy into the handoff doc):
- incident id: svc-infer-eu-1861345678
- timeline: start 1861345678, mitigation routing 1861345785, residual errors <2% by 1861345810, monitoring in progress until 1861345924
- customer impact: hosted api users in eu-west saw ~1–2 minute elevated failure window and some streaming truncations. Dedicated customers unaffected.
- action items: devon to run postmortem root-cause (kernel OOM path), olivia to finalize status page and customer note, jamal to calculate SLA credits and open billing case, li to triage support tickets and notify customers as needed.

li: I'm drafting customer notification for impacted tenants — short, empathetic, and actionable. Draft below for review:

li: ```Customer notification (draft):
Hi —
We experienced a short service disruption affecting API requests to our eu-west region on 2026-04-12 between ~10:01 and 10:03 UTC which caused some requests to fail. We routed traffic to standby capacity and services have returned to normal.
We’re investigating the root cause and will follow up with a post-incident report.
If you rely on streaming responses, please check for any truncated sessions and re-request if needed.
We will assess SLA credit eligibility and reach out to impacted accounts with next steps.
Thanks for your patience — Redwood Support
```

maria: wording looks good — add a link to the support ticket and a contact alias (support@redwood.ai) in the final send.

jamal: once I get the exported logs (devon), I’ll run the SLA calculator. Tentative plan: offer pro-rated credit for the affected minutes for customers on hosted plans per the SLA table. For large enterprise accounts on dedicated where there was no impact, no credit.

devon: exporting request logs now — expected delivery 1861346010 (I will push a CSV to the shared folder with columns: customer_id, route, timestamp, status_code, token_count, session_id).

maria: closing notes for now — monitoring looks stable. If anyone sees regression ping here. We should also trigger a postmortem runbook and schedule RCA. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident marked as mitigated at 1861345924 (status: restored->monitoring).

jamal: ack — will follow up with billing case updates and draft customer-specific compensation messages once logs are in.

li: I'll send the customer notification to the three tenants now and include a note that we'll follow up with specific compensation info. Sending in 2m.

olivia: adding postmortem task to the incidents board and assigning to @devon and @maria.

maria: thanks all — handoff complete for this thread.
